what_happened: Job 20261116-041223-m3vc was a code job to show per-stage duration and main reason in `athena status`. It failed in planning, before any code was written, in round 1 of 5. The plan still broke Athena's own plan rules after 2 mechanical revisions. One major finding is listed. The demonstration for behavior criterion 3 cites a command the verifier may not run: `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <job>/evidence`. No acceptance criteria or checks are listed as unmet or failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planner is not shown which commands the verifier may run as demonstrations. The command rule is checked by code only after the plan is written. The planner then writes the natural demonstration, which is running the CLI on a snapshot. The mechanical repair budget is small (2 revisions), and the repair step seems to fix format only, not which commands are allowed. A defect the code can detect exactly therefore ends the whole job, and the planning spend is lost.
other_causes: The request asked for a status display change, and the natural demonstration is to run the status command. Nothing steers the planner to a verifier-runnable form, such as a test that calls the rendering function.
open_hypotheses: The input does not show which plan rule was broken. It could be the allowed-command rule or the one-demonstration-per-criterion rule. Only the critic's finding about the command is listed.
The input does not show what the 2 mechanical revisions changed or why they did not fix the command.
It is unknown whether the verifier's command policy is too strict for a read-only `cargo run` of the status command.
contradictions: The earlier class 7k8t describes the violation surviving to the last planning round with no repair step. Here the job failed in round 1 of 5, after 2 mechanical revisions, so a repair step did exist.
The event lists a critic major finding, so this may not be a purely mechanical format defect.
prevention: Run the same code check that finds disallowed demonstration commands on each plan draft, and feed the exact offending command and the list of allowed demonstration forms back to the planner inside the mechanical-revision step. Also put the allowed list in the planner's brief up front. A command-rule defect would then be fixed in revision, or never written. The job would not end failed in round 1 of 5 with 4 rounds unused.
proposed_request: Make planning avoid demonstration commands the verifier may not run. (1) Put the list of command forms the verifier may run for a demonstration into the planner's brief. (2) When the plan's mechanical check finds a demonstration command outside that list, the revision step must name the criterion and the offending command and give the allowed forms. (3) Mechanical revisions must not use up the planning rounds that the critic has for design findings. (4) Acceptance: a test that feeds a plan whose demonstration is `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <job>/evidence` and shows the plan is revised to an allowed demonstration (for example a test that calls the status rendering function), not failed. Add a test that a plan with only allowed commands passes unchanged. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
